title_en: Decision of the Supreme People's Court on the Establishment of the Haikou and Xiamen Maritime Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Decision on Establishing Haikou and Xiamen Maritime Courts

Fa (Jiao) Fa [1990] No. 4

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and all Maritime Courts:

To meet the needs of China's economic construction and opening to the outside world, and in accordance with the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Establishing Maritime Courts in Coastal Port Cities, it is hereby decided to establish Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court.

Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court are at the same level as the local intermediate people's courts, and internally establish the Maritime Trial Division, the Admiralty Trial Division, the Research Office, and the General Office, among other organs.

Haikou Maritime Court has jurisdiction over first-instance maritime and admiralty cases arising within the ports and waters under the jurisdiction of Hainan Province, as well as within the islands and waters of the Xisha, Zhongsha, Nansha, and Huangyan Island. Xiamen Maritime Court has jurisdiction over first-instance maritime and admiralty cases arising within the following area: the extended sea areas from the junction of Fujian Province and Guangdong Province in the south to the junction of Fujian Province and Zhejiang Province in the north, including the southern part of the East China Sea, Taiwan Province, offshore islands, and ports under the jurisdiction of Fujian Province. Appeals against first-instance judgments of Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court shall be under the jurisdiction of the Hainan High People's Court and the Fujian High People's Court, respectively.

The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Scope of Case Acceptance by Maritime Courts, as promulgated, shall apply to Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court.

In accordance with the provisions of Articles 2 and 4 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Establishing Maritime Courts in Coastal Port Cities, Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court shall be responsible and report on their work to the Standing Committees of the Haikou and Xiamen Municipal People's Congresses, respectively, and their trial work shall be supervised by the Hainan High People's Court and the Fujian High People's Court, respectively. The Presidents of Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court shall be nominated by the Chairmen of the Standing Committees of the Haikou and Xiamen Municipal People's Congresses, respectively, for appointment or removal by the Standing Committees of the Municipal People's Congresses. The Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, Deputy Division Chiefs, Judges, and Members of the Judicial Committees shall be nominated by the Presidents of Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court for appointment or removal by the Standing Committees of the Haikou and Xiamen Municipal People's Congresses, respectively.

Haikou Maritime Court and Xiamen Maritime Court shall commence accepting cases on March 10 and March 25, 1990, respectively. Cases already accepted prior to this date by Guangzhou Maritime Court and Shanghai Maritime Court shall not be transferred, and appeals in such cases shall still be tried by the Guangdong High People's Court and the Shanghai High People's Court.

March 2, 1990
